Looke vvhether the mo{{ls}}t cha{{ls}}t and {{ls}}acred {{ls}}entences of Gods holy vvord, be not turned of many, into mirth, mockerie, amorous ballets & dete{{ls}}table letters of loue and leudnes: their delicate rimes, tunes, and tran{{ls}}lations much encrea{{ls}}ing the {{ls}}ame.

{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Scriptures erroneou{{ls}}ly expounded according to euery vvicked mans priuate fan{{ls}}ie.}}This fall of good life & prophaning the diuine my{{ls}}teries, euery body {{ls}}eeth: but the great corruption & decay of faith hereby, none {{ls}}ee but vvi{{ls}}e men, who onely knovv, that, vvere the Scriptures neuer {{ls}}o truely tran{{ls}}lated, yet Heretikes and ill men that follovv their ovvne {{ls}}pirit and knovv nothing, but their priuate fanta{{ls}}ie, and not the {{ls}}en{{ls}}e of the holy Church and Doctors, mu{{ls}}t needes abu{{ls}}e them to their damnation: and that the curious {{ls}}imple and *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''1 Cor. 2.''}} {{ls}}en{{ls}}ual men vvhich haue no ta{{ls}}t of the things that be of the Spirit of God, may of infinite places take occa{{ls}}ion of pernicious errors. for though the letter or text haue no error, yet ({{ls}}aith S. Ambro{{ls}}e) the Arrian, or (as vve may novv {{ls}}peake) the Caluinian interpretation hath errors. ''lib. 2 ad Gratianum ca. 1.'' and Tertullian {{ls}}aith, ''The {{ls}}en{{ls}}e adulterated is as perilous as the {{ls}}tyle corrupted. De Præ{{ls}}cript.'' S. Hilarie al{{ls}}o {{ls}}peaketh thus: ''Here{{ls}}ie ri{{ls}}eth about the vnder{{ls}}tanding, not about the vvriting: the fault is in the {{ls}}en{{ls}}e, not in the vvord. lib. 2. de Trinit. in principio.'' and S. Augu{{ls}}tine {{ls}}aith, that many hold the {{ls}}criptures as they doe the Sacraments, ''ad {{ls}}peciem, & non ad {{ls}}alutem: to the outvvard {{ls}}hevv, and not to {{ls}}aluation. de Bapti{{ls}}. cont. Donat. lib. 3. ca. 19.'' Finally all Sect-mai{{ls}}ters and rauening vvolues, yea *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 4.''}} the diuels them {{ls}}elues {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Al Heretikes pretend Scriptures.}}pretend Scriptures, alleage Scriptures, and vvholy {{ls}}hroud them {{ls}}elues in Scriptures, as in the wooll and flee{{ls}}e of the {{ls}}imple {{ls}}heepe. Vvhereby the vulgar, in the{{ls}}e daies of generall di{{ls}}putes, can not but be in extreme danger of error, though their bookes vvere truely tran{{ls}}lated, and vvere truely in them {{ls}}elues Gods ovvne vvord in deede.

{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Scriptures haue been fal{{ls}}ely and heretically tran{{ls}}lated into the vulgar tongues, and {{ls}}undrie other vvaies {{ls}}acrilegiou{{ls}}ly abu{{ls}}ed, and {{ls}}o giuen to the people to reade.}}But the ca{{ls}}e novv is more lamentable: for the Prote{{ls}}tants and {{ls}}uch as S. Paul calleth ''ambulantes in a{{ls}}tutia,''{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''2 Cor. 4.''}} ''vvalking in deceitfulnes,'' haue {{ls}}o abu{{ls}}ed the people and many other in the vvorld, not vnvvi{{ls}}e, that by their fal{{ls}}e tran{{ls}}lations they haue in {{ls}}teede of Gods Lavv and Te{{ls}}tament, & for Chri{{ls}}tes vvritten vvill and vvord, giuen them their ovvne vvicked vvriting and phanta{{ls}}ies, mo{{ls}}t {{ls}}hamefully in all their ver{{ls}}ions Latin, Engli{{ls}}h, and other tonges, corrupting both the letter and {{ls}}en{{ls}}e by fal{{ls}}e tran{{ls}}lation, adding, detracting, altering, tran{{ls}}po{{ls}}ing, pointing, and all other guileful meanes: {{ls}}pecially vvhere it {{ls}}erueth for the aduantage of their priuate opinions. for vvhich, they are bold al{{ls}}o, partly to di{{ls}}authori{{ls}}e quite, partly to make doubtful, diuers vvhole bookes allovved for Canonical Scripture by the vniuer{{ls}}al Church of God this thou{{ls}}and yeres and vpward: to alter al the authentical and Eccle{{ls}}ia{{ls}}tical vvordes v{{ls}}ed {{ls}}ithence our Chri{{ls}}tianitie, into nevv prophane nouelties of {{ls}}peaches agreable to their doctrine: to change the titles of vvorkes, to put out the names of the authors, *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''* Beza annot. in c. 1. Lu. v. 78.''}} to charge the very Euangeli{{ls}}t vvith follovving vntrue tran{{ls}}lation, to adde whole {{ls}}entences proper to their {{ls}}ect, into their p{{ls}}almes in meter, *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''* See the tenth article of their Creede in meter.''}} euen {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Al this their dealing is noted (as occa{{ls}}ion {{ls}}erueth) in the Annotations vpon this Te{{ls}}tament: and more at large in a booke lately made purpo{{ls}}ely of that matter, called, ''A'' {{sc|di{{ls}}coverie}} ''&c.''}}into the very Creede in rime. al vvhich the poore deceiued people {{ls}}ay and {{ls}}ing as though they vvere Gods ovvne vvord, being in deede through {{ls}}uch {{ls}}acrilegious treacherie, made the Diuels vvord

To {{ls}}ay nothing of their intolerable liberty and licence to change the accu{{ls}}tomed callings of God, Angel, men, places, & things v{{ls}}ed by the Apo{{ls}}tles and all antiquitie, in Greeke, Latin, and all other languages of Chri{{ls}}tian Nations, into nevv names, {{ls}}ometimes fal{{ls}}ely, and alvvaies ridiculou{{ls}}ly and for o{{ls}}tentation taken of the Hebrues: to frame and fine the phra{{ls}}es of holy Scriptures after the forme of prophane writers, {{ls}}ticking not, for the {{ls}}ame to {{ls}}upply, adde, alter or dimini{{ls}}h as freely as if they tran{{ls}}lated Liuie, Virgil, or Terence. {{hws|Ha|Hauing}}<noinclude>{{continues|uing}}</noinclude>
